liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (3 reviews): Bird Song is described as wildly intense; Bird Song jam goes farther out, called one of the best jammed versions ever [22][23][24]
- **CC Rider** (1 review): CC Rider is called solid and a personal all-time favorite [19]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): Reviewer asks whether the second-encore Good Lovin' circulates, noting it is missing from their Bobby Good Lovin' collection [20]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): China Cat Sunflower into I Know You Rider closes the first set [21]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain opens the second set energetically [21]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Wharf Rat is singled out as amazing [21]
- **It's All Over Now, Baby Blue** (1 review): The Baby Blue version is especially nice [22]
- **Greatest Story Ever Told** (1 review): Greatest Story Ever Told is described as near perfect [23]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd81-09-12 s1t01 Crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd81-09-12 s1t02 Shakedown Street**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd81-09-12 s1t03 Greatest Story Ever Told**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd81-09-12 s1t04 Friend Of The Devil**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd81-09-12 s1t05 El Paso**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd81-09-12 s1t06 Bird Song**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd81-09-12 s1t07 Cassidy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]
- **gd81-09-12 s1t08 Tennessee Jed**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [30]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-09-12.142836.fob.senn421.wise.miller.clugston.flac1648** (recommended): audience recording; 26 songs; 200 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1981-09-12.158148.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 23 songs; 198 min [3]
- **gd1981-09-12.nak700.anon-poris-severson.LMPP.95391.flac16**: source not stated; 24 songs; 197 min; rated 4.71/5 by 7 [6]
- **gd1981-09-12.nak700.martin.warner.23729.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 199 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [9]
- **gd81-09-12.aud.wise.25317.shnf**: audience recording; 22 songs; 190 min; rated 4.46/5 by 13 [15]. Said about its sound: Audience recording conveys the excitement of a crowd seeing the band at its peak [24]
- **gd81-09-12.wise.munder.7091.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 188 min; rated 4.38/5 by 16 [16]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says Jim Wise's audience recording turned out surprisingly well given the taping circumstances [18]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended these Greek shows in person [18]
- Double encore came after Bob got the crowd to fetch Phil [19]
- Reviewer says the Greek had great acoustics for the Dead and the band loved playing there [22]
- Crowd reaction shows fans knew they were seeing something special; Bay Area crowds were relaxed, letting the band play [25]
- Reviewer says these were the first Greek shows since the 1960s [26]
- Start times: 7 p.m. Friday, 5 p.m. Saturday, and about 1 p.m. Sunday [26]
- Crowd reaction shows fans knew they were seeing something special; Bay Area crowds were relaxed, letting the band play [28]
- The Greek Theater shows were a tapers' choice run the taper holds dear [6]
- Reviewer calls it possibly the most uncompromising show of the 80s, with every song given special treatment [23]
- Reviewer considers this the gem of the Greek run and among the best shows they've heard [25]
- Reviewer considers this the gem of the Greek run and among the best shows they've heard [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-09-12.142836.fob.senn421.wise.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: flac16/48kHz ; Source Info: Jim Wise's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UD-XLII); Transfer Info: Master Cassettes… [1]. Also: Jim Wise recorded the show; this is a fresh transcription of his FOB audience master, coordinated by Charlie Miller [1]
- **gd1981-09-12.158148.akg.se5.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Wiseman and Scott Clugston; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG SE-5E mics with CE-1 cardioid capsules > Sony TC-D5 (Maxell UDXLII 90) [3]. Also: Jim Wise's Sennheiser 421 source patches crowd, song openings and gaps, including Wharf Rat's end and Eyes Of The World's beginning [3]
- **gd1981-09-12.nak700.anon-poris-severson.LMPP.95391.flac16**: taped by anonymous taper, Jamie Poris, Mark Severson; transferred by Brian Green and Evan K.; source: 3 Nakamichi 700's (l & R-Cross Cardiod, 6db Bass EQ, 75 Deg angle, center-omni straight at stage, 40 deg up) 40 feet from stage, dead center > 3 mic mixer(made… [6]. Also: Anonymous taper's group of friends made the tapes; he waited most of the weekend in line for the best spot [6]
- **gd1981-09-12.nak700.martin.warner.23729.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Steven Martin; transferred by (EAC > SHN by Jack Warner); source: modified Nakamichi CM-700 mics > Sony TC-D5M > MAC (Maxell metal tape) [9]. Also: Main source is Jim Wise's Sennheiser 421 mics into a Sony TC-D5, transferred via MAC to CD; Encore patched from another audience source, probably two Sony ECM-33P mics to Sony TC-D5, reels, then DAT [9]
- **gd81-09-12.aud.wise.25317.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; transferred by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421's [15]
- **gd81-09-12.wise.munder.7091.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sennheiser 421's [16]

claims.text: Reviewer says Jim Wise's audience recording turned out surprisingly well given the taping circumstances
Reviewer attended these Greek shows in person
CC Rider is called solid and a personal all-time favorite
Double encore came after Bob got the crowd to fetch Phil
Reviewer asks whether the second-encore Good Lovin' circulates, noting it is missing from their Bobby Good Lovin' collection
China Cat Sunflower into I Know You Rider closes the first set
Scarlet Begonias into Fire On The Mountain opens the second set energetically
Wharf Rat is singled out as amazing
Bird Song is described as wildly intense

claims.text: The Baby Blue version is especially nice
Reviewer says the Greek had great acoustics for the Dead and the band loved playing there
Bird Song jam goes farther out, called one of the best jammed versions ever
Greatest Story Ever Told is described as near perfect
Reviewer calls it possibly the most uncompromising show of the 80s, with every song given special treatment
Bird Song and Cassidy are described as incredibly hot
Audience recording conveys the excitement of a crowd seeing the band at its peak
Crowd reaction shows fans knew they were seeing something special; Bay Area crowds were relaxed, letting the band play
Reviewer considers this the gem of the Greek run and among the best shows they've heard
Reviewer says these were the first Greek shows since the 1960s

Jim Wise recorded the show; this is a fresh transcription of his FOB audience master, coordinated by Charlie Miller
Source cassettes and transfer came from Scott Wiseman, using AKG microphones

Anonymous taper's group of friends made the tapes; he waited most of the weekend in line for the best spot
The Greek Theater shows were a tapers' choice run the taper holds dear
Main source is Jim Wise's Sennheiser 421 mics into a Sony TC-D5, transferred via MAC to CD
Encore patched from another audience source, probably two Sony ECM-33P mics to Sony TC-D5, reels, then DAT
